title: The Infamous Edgar Haircut in Midland-Odessa - NewsBreak
text:
By Dominique ,
11 hours ago
In the heart of West Texas, a new style trend has emerged within the past few years: the Edgar haircut.
Characterized by sharp lines, a blunt fringe, and clean fades, the Edgar has gained popularity among young men in Midland and Odessa , serving as more than just a haircut—it’s a statement.
Download the KZBT-KGEE Mobile App Now Edgar Haircut Origins Originally from Latino and Chicano communities in South Texas and Northern Mexico, the Edgar cut—sometimes called the “Takuache” haircut—symbolizes cultural pride, individuality, and confidence.
This style typically appeals to youth seeking a bold, low-maintenance look.
Aleksandar Andreev via Unsplash Edgar Judgement and Stereotype For whatever reason, this style of haircut seems to draw much attention. Granted, this is not the first haircut to be associated with a particular stereotype, but many assume people who rock the Edgar are criminals or people with bad intentions.
But why?
Why does this haircut rub people the wrong way? Some say it is a ridiculous look, while others may see it as simply a bad hairstyle.
The “Edgar” in Midland-Odessa Local barbershops are seeing increasing requests for various Edgar styles, from high fades with textured tops to classic blunt fringes.
Many clients add personal touches, like shaved designs or pastel dye jobs, to make the look their own.
For many young men in Midland and Odessa, the Edgar reflects a blend of tradition and modernity, honoring cultural roots while embracing contemporary fashion.
Read More: Barbershops in Midland-Odessa Become Safe Haven For Men
As fall arrives, expect to see the Edgar cut dominating local hotspots throughout the Permian Basin.
Regardless of personal opinions, one thing is clear: the Edgar haircut is here to stay, whether you like it or not.

Gallery Credit: Taylor Linzinmeir Paul Natkin, Getty Images Axl Rose, Before When Axl Rose first popped up on the rock scene as the founder of Guns ‘N’ Roses, he was sporting the typical uniform of all rockers at the time: long hair with a little bit of fringe and just a dash of grease. He’d occasionally add a bandana around his forehead to complete the look. KMazur, Getty Images/WireImage Axl Rose, After And then came the early 2000s. That’s when Rose unveiled a new look to the world: a full head of braids. Needless to say, fans of Guns ‘N’ Roses were not fans of the new hairstyle. Some criticized the look for not being “rock” enough (whatever that’s supposed to mean) and others circulated rumors that Rose was going bald and the braids were an effort to hide a failed transplant surgery. But that didn’t matter to Rose, as he told Jimmy Kimmel in 2012 he was not ashamed of the look. Fin Costello, Getty Images Ozzy Osbourne, Before Ozzy Osbourne has one of the most memorable looks of any rocker in history. His dark, slightly wavy hair that’s parted in the middle and flows just past his shoulders has been a staple for Osbourne for decades. YouTube Ozzy Osbourne, After Everyone remembers that one time in 1982 when Ozzy Osbourne bit the head off of a bat while on stage. But not many people remember that around the same time the rocker shaved off all of his hair. He shared a photo from his bald era a few years ago on his social media accounts, and fans wondered whether or not they had simply erased that time from their brains, as no one seemed to remember it happening. Icon and Image, Michael Ochs Archive/Getty Images Metallica, Before When Metallica was born in 1981, original members James Hetfield, Lars Ulrich, Kirk Hammett and Cliff Burton each rocked the same look: lusciously teased out, long hair with bangs —perfect for headbanging. Niels Van Iperen, Getty Images/Hulton Archive Metallica, After But when they began to do press for their 1996 record Load , they had all gone with a shorter look. It became a point of contention for some fans, accusing the band of selling out. Ulrich made it clear in a 2017 interview that they did not, in fact, all go to the barber shop together and get a 4-for-1 discount. Instead, they simply all individually decided to cut their hair between ‘93 and ‘96. Rune Hellestad - Corbis, Corbis Entertainment/Getty Images Max Cavalera, Before In 1997, Soulfly and Sepulta legend Max Cavalera began growing one massive loc. A mono-lock, if you will. The loc almost had a celebrity status of its own, as fans would occasionally go up to the musician just to see it up close and personal. YouTube Max Cavalera And then one day in 2020, Gloria Cavalera, Max’s wife and manager, posted a photo of the severed loc on her Instagram account. She wrote, “It must be snowing in hell today!” Many of the comments under the post mourned the loss of the iconic look, while one person pointed out, “I could retread my tire with that bad boy.” Evan Agostini, Getty Images Davey Havok, Before AFI’s Davey Havok rocked scene-level fringe complete with blond highlights, resembling the asymmetrical bob of soccer mom’s everywhere, during the mainstream peak of their career. It was like he was in competition with Cris Angel to see who had the best swoop. Rise Records Davey Havok, After He then traded in the fashions of the early 2000s for something a little more retro: a mullet. The look was unleashed on the cover of Kerrang ! in March 2021. To quote Havok himself, “Everything ends. And my endings tend to be eternal.” YouTube: Paramore Hayley Williams, Before Hayley Williams has probably worn every shade of hair color under the rainbow. During the Riot! era, she sported bright red hair, then went to orange, teal, electric blue and finally to a gold and green duo. She even has her own hair color line called Good Dye Young. Alberto E. Rodriguez, Getty Images Hayley Williams, After But during her After Laughter era, she ditched the bright colors for a sleek platinum blonde. She told Entertainment Weekly that hair is a “very emotional thing” for her. When she spoke to her colorist, she said that she needed a “reset.” Only time will tell if Williams goes through another phase of bright colors. “When it’s time for Neon Hayley to come back to life, she will,” she says. “But right now, this is me." Michael Ochs Archives, Stringer/Getty Images Phil Spector, Before You may be wondering why we included Phil Spector in this list. After all, the producer’s hair throughout most of his career was not really news-worthy, in fact it was a little dull. He mostly kept his brown hair short, sometimes with a comb over (and now we know what secrets he was hiding under there). Phil Spector, After And then came 2009. For some reason, Spector decided that a murder trial would be the perfect time to try out a few new looks. With the help of some wigs, Spector came into court with a blond bowlcut one day and a giant blond afro the next. Perhaps it was a failed attempt to distract the jury of his crime? Pool, Getty Images (2) Phil Spector, After And then came 2009. For some reason, Spector decided that a murder trial would be the perfect time to try out a few new looks. With the help of some wigs, Spector came into court with a blond bowlcut one day and a giant blond afro the next. Perhaps it was a failed attempt to distract the jury of his crime? Johnny Louis, Getty Images BONUS: That Time Claudio Sanchez Tricked Everyone Into Thinking He Lopped Off His Luscious Locks When Coheed and Cambria frontman Claudio Sanchez posted a photo of himself on Instagram in 2017, appearing to have cut off all his hair, fans thought it was the end of an era. It was the talk of the town, with news outlets, including Loudwire , covering the new look (afterall, his hair is arguably the glue that holds that band together). Thankfully, he revealed it was all just a joke while performing a day later. Today, his hair is as lucious as ever. Don’t ever change, Claudio. Don’t ever change.
